context: First decide between three dispositions and record the choice with its rationale: (a) suppress the footer on all GitHub surfaces and accept that agent comments under the owner account are indistinguishable from human ones; (b) keep a disclosure but make it terse and consistent across comment and PR-body surfaces, replacing the two divergent strings with one; (c) keep the footer but stop posting as the owner, routing agent comments through a bot identity where attribution is implicit. Then encode the decision as a repository rule adjacent to [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] in AGENTS.md, phrased the same way the trailer rule is -- a tool or harness convention is not authorization -- so it binds agents regardless of what their harness instructs. Keep it to a few lines; AGENTS.md is byte-ceilinged. Enforcement is advisory only: no repo-side hook can intercept a GitHub API call, so do not claim prevention. If mechanical detection is wanted, the honest form is a scheduled or on-comment workflow that flags posts carrying the footer, which detects after the fact rather than preventing.
description: Agent-authored GitHub posts are appearing with a trailing horizontal rule and the italic line 'Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)'. Live instance: the closing comment on PR #1494 (issue comment 5174430128) ends with exactly that footer. ROOT CAUSE: the agent harness's GitHub-integration instructions mandate it, in the same way the commit trailer was mandated -- the operating instructions state that every comment, review, review reply, or issue comment the agent authors MUST end with the Claude Code attribution footer, appended verbatim as the final lines of the body, and that the agent should include it even when the posting tool also adds one because duplicates are stripped server-side. A second, differently-worded variant is mandated for PR bodies ('Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)' plus a session URL), which is why PR #1494's description carries a footer that does not match the comment footer. This is repo-external in origin and identical in class to the Co-Authored-By trailer, but NOT covered by the existing control: [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] and the commit-msg gate added in #1494 govern COMMIT messages only, and nothing governs GitHub comment or PR-body surfaces. It is also more visible than the commit trailer because these posts are made through the maintainer's own GitHub account (author_association OWNER), so the footer renders as the repository owner announcing that their own comment was machine-generated. DECISION REQUIRED, do not silently strip: the footer is currently the ONLY signal distinguishing an agent-authored comment from a human one on an OWNER-attributed post. Removing it without replacing the signal trades a noisy disclosure for no disclosure.

anti_patterns.dont: Claim a repo-side hook or CI job prevents the footer
anti_patterns.instead: State the rule as binding on agents and, if wanted, add after-the-fact detection that flags rather than blocks
anti_patterns.why: The footer is appended by the agent when calling the GitHub API; no repository-side control sits in that path

anti_patterns.dont: Fix only the comment footer and leave the PR-body variant
anti_patterns.instead: Cover comment, review, review reply, issue comment and PR body in one rule
anti_patterns.why: Two differently-worded footers are mandated for two surfaces, so fixing one leaves the other appearing and looks like the rule did not work

anti_patterns.dont: Strip the footer without deciding what replaces it as a disclosure signal
anti_patterns.instead: Record an explicit disposition; if disclosure is dropped, say so deliberately rather than as a side effect of reducing noise
anti_patterns.why: These comments post under the maintainer's own GitHub account, so with no footer an agent-authored comment is indistinguishable from a human one
